name: Beach
notes: Sandy beaches above the tide line: salt- and sand-tolerant pioneers (creeping vines, succulent herbs, sea rocket) with coconut, screw pine and sea grape on tropical strands and sea buckthorn/pine on temperate ones. Drawn on Indo-Pacific and Caribbean strands, Atlantic Europe and eastern North America.

canopy.name: Coconut palm
canopy.source: Cocos nucifera, pantropical strand palm (Indo-Pacific origin), sandy coasts, 15-30 m — Wikipedia / POWO

canopy.name: Screw pine
canopy.source: Pandanus tectorius, Indo-Pacific coasts (Hawaii to Australia), beach margins with prop roots, 4-14 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Sea grape
canopy.source: Coccoloba uvifera, Caribbean and Florida beaches, round leathery leaves, gnarled 3-10 m tree — Wikipedia / IFAS

canopy.name: Beach she-oak
canopy.source: Casuarina equisetifolia, SE Asia/Australia/Pacific beaches (widely naturalised), needle-like branchlets, 6-35 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Maritime pine
canopy.source: Pinus pinaster, western Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts (Landes), stabilised beach sands, 20-35 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Beach naupaka
shrub.source: Scaevola taccada, Indo-Pacific tropical beaches, succulent-leaved mounding shrub 1-3 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Sea buckthorn
shrub.source: Hippophae rhamnoides, Eurasian coasts (North Sea, Baltic) and steppes, silver-leaved thorny shrub with orange berries, 1-6 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Beach heliotrope
shrub.source: Heliotropium (Tournefortia) arboreum, Indo-Pacific beach crests, silvery-leaved shrub/small tree 1-5 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Wax myrtle
shrub.source: Morella cerifera, SE US Atlantic/Gulf coasts, back-beach thickets, evergreen shrub 2-8 m — Wikipedia / USDA

ground.name: Beach morning glory
ground.source: Ipomoea pes-caprae, pantropical beach pioneer vine (goat's foot), creeping over open sand, 0.1-0.3 m tall — Wikipedia

ground.name: Sea rocket
ground.source: Cakile maritima, European/N African strandline annual (C. edentula in N America), fleshy leaves, lilac flowers, 0.1-0.4 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Sea purslane
ground.source: Sesuvium portulacastrum, pantropical beaches and salt flats, succulent mat-forming herb, 5-20 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Sea holly
ground.source: Eryngium maritimum, European Atlantic and Mediterranean beaches, spiny blue-grey rosette 20-60 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Beach spinifex
ground.source: Spinifex sericeus, Australian and NZ beaches, silvery stoloniferous foredune grass 30-80 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Bitter panicgrass
ground.source: Panicum amarum, US Atlantic and Gulf beaches, blue-green clumping upper-beach grass 0.5-1.5 m — USDA Plants
